alignments.note: Future passive with its auxiliaries as rule 9 helpers; head on the lexical participle *filled* rather than on *shall* or *be*.

Future passive of ταπεινόω rendered by the resultative *shall be brought low*. Rule 17 heads a resultative on the meaning-bearing complement (*make straight* heads on *straight*), and rule 91's test agrees: *brought* answers to no element of the lexeme, while *low* is what glosses it. A head on *brought* is not defensible under rule 17's refusal of the merely finite or auxiliary word.

Substantival article before an adjective takes the English determiner *the* under rules 19 and 22; the adjective keeps its own bare word. No supplied nominal stands here for rule 102 to give the article, so *the* is all it carries.
ἔσται with εἰς rendered as *shall become*; the auxiliary is a rule 9 helper and the head is the lexical verb *become*.

The Septuagintal εἰς of result is absorbed into the ASV's *shall become straight*: no English word answers to the preposition, so rule 36's closing test leaves it its own unrepresented unit. Reading *become* as realizing the preposition alongside the verb is the competing analysis, but the copula's own English is already complete and rule 27 forbids splitting it.

Predicate adjective *straight*. Variant SBLGNT.LUK.3.5.v003 is underdetermined with r00-base and r01 both compatible; the projection's reading is translated either way, so no textual decision is made here (rule 12).
Article takes the English determiner *the*; the ASV construes the phrase attributively (*the rough ways*), so the article is the noun phrase's determiner under rule 19.

Second result εἰς, likewise unrealized: the ASV writes only *the rough ways smooth*, with no preposition word anywhere. Rule 36 leaves it empty on the same terms as s014, which is rule 24's habit of analysing the two parallel clauses alike.
Bare noun *ways*; the determiner stands on the article of the preceding phrase, which the ASV has fused with this one.

review_notes: The ASV recasts the two εἰς clauses as predicate complements (*shall become straight*, *ways smooth*), so both prepositions are unrepresented under rule 36 rather than folded into a verb or a noun.
s009 heads on *low* under rule 17's resultative clause, not on *brought*.
s017 governs the expressed noun ὁδούς across the intervening adjective and takes the plain *the* (rules 19 and 57); it is not displaced by anything.
